evidence.note: Under a fixed inference budget, training data generated by a weaker-but-cheaper (WC) language model consistently produces better-performing reasoner students than data from a stronger-but-more-expensive (SE) model, across knowledge distillation, self-improvement, and a novel weak-to-strong learning paradigm -- challenging the default practice of sourcing synthetic training data from the most powerful available model.
evidence.title: Smaller, Weaker, Yet Better: Training LLM Reasoners via Compute-Optimal Sampling
